claims.text: The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy is produced by conventional melting and casting.
Undoped HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
Undoped HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa and a terminal strain of 13.5%.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has limited tensile ductility in its undoped state.
An O-2-like oxygen content can be introduced during arc melting of HfZrTiTa0.53 by adjusting oxygen partial pressure.
Controlled interstitial oxygen doping will produce ordered oxygen complexes in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Ordered oxygen complexes impede dislocation motion in a controlled manner.
Impeded dislocation motion from ordered oxygen complexes enhances strain hardening.
The enhanced strain hardening delays tensile necking.
Controlled oxygen doping will improve the tensile ductility and uniform elongation of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The uniform tensile elongation will increase from approximately 13.5% to approximately 18–20%.
The oxygen-doped alloy will retain a yield strength of approximately 800–1100 MPa.
Oxygen doping will preserve the impact-triggered chemical energy release of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed ductility benefit applies at room temperature under quasi-static tension at approximately 1×10^-3 s^-1.
Behavior at substantially higher temperatures or strain rates may differ because of altered diffusion or dynamic strain-aging effects.
The cited (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98O2 alloy exhibited approximately 1138 MPa yield strength and approximately 20% tensile elongation at room temperature and 1×10^-3 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% value is introduced as terminal strain alongside compressive properties, but the predicted outcome treats it as the baseline uniform tensile elongation. Terminal compressive strain and uniform tensile elongation are not interchangeable measurements.

The low end of the predicted range, 18%, is only a 4.5 percentage-point increase over 13.5%, whereas the falsification rule requires at least a 5 percentage-point increase. Thus, part of the stated predicted range would itself satisfy the stated falsification condition.
A yield-strength range extending to 1100 MPa is described as close to or only slightly above the 786 MPa baseline, although 1100 MPa is approximately 40% higher.
